- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) or negative (0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.7) but model forecasts decline, adjust downward bias by 0.5–1.5% per sentiment unit above 0.6.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per period.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-periods (last 5–7 days) — apply downward correction of 1–2% for final 5–7 forecast days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.6 → 0.0 → 0.6), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% lag correction to forecast 2–3 periods ahead.
